newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end little changed.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end little changed.

text.p: Key September Euroyen futures ended Tuesday's TIFFE day session little changed in thin trade.
The September closed up 0.01 at 99.32 after trading between 99.31 and 99.33. Volume was 12,228 contracts.

A relatively stable Tokyo stock market after recent wild fluctuations and a cautious mood ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before a Senate committee on Tuesday were responsible for the slow trading, traders said.
"As stocks were relatively stable today, there was no incentive to push Euroyen futures in either direction," a city bank trader said.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares closed down 122.18 points, or 0.70 percent, at 17,358.16.
If the Nikkei falls sharply below 17,000 in coming sessions, the September contract may test higher levels, traders said.
A weak stock market is considered supportive for Euroyen futures as it underscores the market's view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will need to maintain its low interest rate policy.
"As the downside risks remain for Tokyo stocks, players are likely to maintain a buy-on-dips stance," said a trader at a long-term credit bank.
"People were reluctant to trade ahead of Greenspan's testimony tonight and BOJ governor's press conference on Wednesday," the city bank trader said.
Market participants were worried about possible wild swings in U.S. bond and stock prices following the Greenspan testimony, traders said.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's news conference is scheduled for 0600 GMT on Wednesday.
In the interbank money market, the key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.49 percent, unchanged from Monday.
The BOJ injected a net 100 billion yen into the money market on Tuesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.53 percent. One-month and two-month CDs were offered at 0.51 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from Monday.
